title: Consistency in art generation tips?
author: mccoypauley
selftext:
TLDR: What are your techniques for keeping art consistency in frontier hosted models? (See the bottom of the post for what I've tried.)

BACKGROUND:

So way back when Stable Diffusion came out, that's where I started with genAI on the open source program Auto1111. I've been following local development since then, as it evolved into SDXL and then Flux and now the plethora of modern models today like Chroma and Qwen Edit, etc (and all  the video-gen models). We moved from Auto1111 -> ComfyUI and it seems to be the standard for local generations.

Anyhow, there was this barrier to getting a really faithful style reproduction post-SDXL, where when the models moved from tag-based prompting to natural language, they lost the association of artist names with tags (in a sense). That is, an SDXL model understood what "Edward Gorey style" meant in a way that none of the modern models do without using LoRAs, and so the problem nowadays is that you can get amazing prompt comprehension, but the style adherence has never been *quite* the same unless you train a LoRA. (I can get into this in more detail, but suffice it to say that an "Edward Gorey" + XYZ other prompt tags rendered by SDXL, despite its shit prompt comprehension, is still way more faithful to style than any frontier model I've encountered and that has something to do with the way the image models are now trained.)

It's why you can spot a Midjourney gen from a ChatGPT gen unless you go to great lengths to tweak the prompt or tweak the image after the fact, whereas local stuff is undetectable (if you create a competent workflow) because it doesn't contain that telltale "slop" bias that each frontier model imparts into your generations.

ANYWAY, that aside:

How are you getting frontier models to stick to a defined style?

What I've tried (in Codex):

* Create a local environment with several fixed sample images representing the style
* Write an elaborate prompt that describes the style and expectations of rendering
* Force the [AGENTS.md](http://AGENTS.md) procedure to be: read the SKILL with the prompt instructions, check the reference material, then do the generation, using a high-reasoning model like Sol High.
* Have a separate subagent act as a critic who compares the reference material to the generated icon, and if it doesn't conform, send it back to the main agent to re-generate until it does.
* Have a separate subagent act as an "implementer" who saves the file in the appropriate format.

I found that this keeps the style on track from drifting if I give it a spreadsheet of art to make (but it doesn't solve the problem I was describing in "background"), BUT it does require at least Sol High. It seems Terra or lower fall can't instruct the underlying image gen model enough to overcome its "slop" bias. 

What have you been doing? Is Ultra or Astra leagues above this? Does it all come back to the underlying image gen model no matter what we use?

comments.author: _raydeStar
comments.body:
one thing i hate about using the image in chat is that it tends to drift, quickly.  

I built a little app for images that holds onto the prompt and holds reference images that help create consistency.  

It's not quite ready for launch yet but it's close... but the idea is 

1) have a prompt

2) have reference images (plural if needed) 

3) use that area for image gen, not a chat window, which notoriously will lose context.

https://preview.redd.it/a8xtzrryrdqh1.png?width=1280&format=png&auto=webp&s=50310fc6270e22c9de7fa532a48d5f2ba3bf17e4

Once reset hits, I can finish it up, but another project superseded it for now.

replies.author: mccoypauley
replies.body: That is super cool. What models is it leveraging under the hood and what reasoning level?

replies.author: _raydeStar
replies.body:
yeah its wild, i dont even run it myself anymore, i just tell codex what to do.  it saws off all the work, and just does it for me.  

Example -- music.  i select the model, it looks up what to do, and sets it up.  Sage attention is a notorious pain in the butt, it can set it up in five minutes.  It's a huge unlock because I can also have it generate full scenes with one prompt.  

ie this one -- [https://markbhall.dev/stillwater/](https://markbhall.dev/stillwater/)

comments.author: Kashmakers
comments.body:
I needed a way for art generation to use my image as a base, and keep the style close to it and draw on top of it. GPT would recreate the image, and local based generation would always create something new and inconsistent. Gemini however, will use your image and draw on top, it is the most consistent out of them all.

Got myself a key for Gemini, and got AI to build me a local host where I can write in a prompt, upload the reference image (with strict instructions built-in to follow the reference image) and it would send the instructions to Gemini to generate the image. It would return with the image.

It works really well, Gemini is able to stay true to my instructions each time I generate an image (versus going to Gemini itself, and once you have one prompt done, the next image generations will drift away from the original prompt).

This only works on existing work though, unsure about completely generating a new image.

comments.author: sannleikur
comments.body: Have you tried keeping the local LoRA generation for style lock and only using the frontier stuff for prompt comprehension on layout, then reconciling? For that telltale frontier, running the output through Magnific with a low-ish creativity setting can strip some of the slop bias without needing to retrain, might be worth a test against your reference set.

replies.body:
